1: //! The pluggable level-generator port: each Backrooms "level" (Level 0
 2: //! offices, Level 34-B grassland, ...) is one implementation.
 3: //!
 4: //! Contract for implementors:
 5: //! * **Seamless tiling** — derive ALL geometry from *world-space* coordinates
 6: //!   (chunk origin + local voxel index), never from chunk-local positions, so
 7: //!   independently generated chunks line up at their borders.
 8: //! * **Walkability** — the ground plane must stay connected: never fully
 9: //!   enclose a region the player could be in. Doorways/gaps must be at least
10: //!   ~1 world unit wide.
11: //! * **Determinism** — same (chunk_pos, seed, config) must always produce the
12: //!   same grid; only the injected [`NoiseProvider`] may be used for variety.
13: //! * Lighting is NOT the generator's job: place `VOXEL_LIGHT` sources and the
14: //!   orchestrating use case runs the BFS lighting pass afterwards.
15: 
16: use crate::domain::entities::voxel_grid::VoxelGrid;
17: use crate::entities::models::Position;
18: use crate::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig;
19: use crate::use_cases::ports::NoiseProvider;
20: 
21: /// Well-known level ids (the `GeneratorConfig::level` / noclip targets).
22: pub const LEVEL_BACKROOMS: u32 = 0;
23: pub const LEVEL_LEGACY_OFFICES: u32 = 1;
24: pub const LEVEL_GRASSLAND: u32 = 34;
25: 
26: pub trait LevelGenerator {
27:     /// Fills one chunk. `chunk_pos` is the chunk origin in world units.
28:     fn generate(
29:         &self,
30:         chunk_pos: Position,
31:         seed: u32,
32:         config: GeneratorConfig,
33:         noise: &dyn NoiseProvider,
34:     ) -> VoxelGrid;
35: }
files.wasm_frontend/src/lib.rs:
1: //! # wasm_frontend — browser client for the vackrooms voxel engine
 2: //!
 3: //! This crate is the *outer rings* of the engine's Clean Architecture when it
 4: //! runs in a browser. The dependency rule points strictly inward:
 5: //!
 6: //! ```text
 7: //! drivers (web-sys, WebGL2, DOM)        <- wasm32 only
 8: //!    |
 9: //! adapters (input mapping, SVO atlas, local chunk source)
10: //!    |
11: //! application (player physics, streaming policy, frame orchestration, ports)
12: //!    |
13: //! vackrooms core (entities + use cases: VoxelGrid, SVO, generation, lighting)
14: //! ```
15: //!
16: //! * `application` and `adapters` are platform-agnostic and unit-tested with
17: //!   plain `cargo test` on the host.
18: //! * `drivers` is the only module that talks to the browser, and it is only
19: //!   compiled for `wasm32`.
20: //! * The `#[wasm_bindgen(start)]` entry point below is the composition root:
21: //!   it wires concrete drivers into the application's ports.
22: 
23: pub mod application;
24: pub mod adapters;
25: 
26: #[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
27: pub mod drivers;
28: 
29: #[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
30: mod entry {
31:     use wasm_bindgen::prelude::*;
32: 
33:     /// Composition root. Runs automatically when the wasm module is
34:     /// instantiated by `static/index.html`.
35:     #[wasm_bindgen(start)]
36:     pub fn start() -> Result<(), JsValue> {
37:         console_error_panic_hook::set_once();
38:         crate::drivers::browser::boot()
39:     }
40: }
files.ARCHITECTURE.md:
1: # Vackrooms — Architecture
  2: 
  3: A voxel-only rendering engine built on **Clean Architecture**, targeting
  4: low-spec hardware. The whole engine — procedural generation, lighting, sparse
  5: voxel octree (SVO) construction, chunk streaming, player physics, and WebGL2
  6: raymarching — compiles to a single ~140 KB WebAssembly module. The browser
  7: runs it; a zero-dependency native HTTP server merely serves the files.
  8: 
  9: ## Rendering family
 10: 
 11: Of the three classical voxel pipeline families (mesh/rasterized,
 12: SVO ray casting, hybrid), this engine implements a **hybrid SVO raymarcher**:
 13: 
 14: 1. **Chunk-level coarse pass** — each resident chunk's AABB is slab-tested
 15:    per fragment and the hits are insertion-sorted by entry distance, so rays
 16:    march the nearest chunk first and exit on the first solid hit.
 17: 2. **Fragment SVO traversal** — stack-based descent through the octree with
 18:    **empty-space skipping**: an air leaf or masked-out octant is exited in a
 19:    single step via its AABB exit plane, never voxel-by-voxel.
 20: 3. **Shading** — packed 24-bit leaf color × BFS-propagated light level,
 21:    face normal from the hit box, exponential distance fog.
 22: 
 23: Low-spec strategy: no depth buffer, no MSAA, nearest-filtered integer
 24: textures, and an **adaptive internal-resolution governor** (0.5×–1.0× backing
 25: store, hysteresis + cooldown) instead of temporal checkerboarding — simpler,
 26: and it degrades smoothly on weak GPUs.
 27: 
 28: ## The dependency rule
 29: 
 30: Source dependencies point inward only. No inner layer names a browser, GPU,
 31: socket, or clock.
 32: 
 33: ```
 34: ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 35: │ FRAMEWORKS & DRIVERS                                               │
 36: │   wasm_frontend/drivers   WebGL2, DOM events, rAF, HUD, console    │
 37: │   src/main.rs             native HTTP server (std::net only)      │
 38: │   src/frameworks_drivers  SimpleNoiseProvider, StdTelemetry        │
 39: │  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │
 40: │  │ INTERFACE ADAPTERS                                           │  │
 41: │  │   src/adapters            OctreeGpuSerializer, VoxelMapper,  │  │
 42: │  │                           JsonPresenter                      │  │
 43: │  │   src/interface_adapters  WebRendererAdapter (presenters)    │  │
 44: │  │   wasm_frontend/adapters  InputCollector, LocalChunkSource   │  │
 45: │  │  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │  │
 46: │  │  │ USE CASES (application business rules)                 │  │  │
 47: │  │  │   src/use_cases           GenerateChunk + ports        │  │  │
 48: │  │  │   src/domain/use_cases    BuildOctree, lighting, maze  │  │  │
 49: │  │  │   wasm_frontend/application  Engine (frame loop),      │  │  │
 50: │  │  │      Player, CollisionWorld, StreamingPolicy, atlas    │  │  │
 51: │  │  │      + ports (RendererPort, ChunkSourcePort)           │  │  │
 52: │  │  │  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │  │  │
 53: │  │  │  │ ENTITIES (enterprise business rules)             │  │  │  │
 54: │  │  │  │   VoxelGrid, SparseVoxelOctree, Position, Grid   │  │  │  │
 55: │  │  │  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │  │  │
 56: │  │  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │  │
 57: │  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │
 58: └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
 59: ```
 60: 
 61: ### Crates
 62: 
 63: | Crate | Role | Targets |
 64: |---|---|---|
 65: | `vackrooms` (root) | Entities + use cases + adapters; native dev-server binary | native **and** wasm32 |
 66: | `wasm_frontend` | Browser client: application/adapters (portable) + drivers (wasm-only) | wasm32 (pure layers test natively) |
 67: | `wasm_raycaster` | Legacy CPU raycaster experiment | kept for reference |
 68: 
 69: The split inside `wasm_frontend` is enforced mechanically: `web-sys`,
 70: `js-sys` and `wasm-bindgen` are `[target.'cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")']`
 71: dependencies, and `drivers/` is `#[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]`. A native
 72: `cargo test` therefore cannot even *see* browser types — the compiler is the
 73: architecture cop.
 74: 
 75: ### Ports (dependency inversion boundaries)
 76: 
 77: | Port | Defined in (inner) | Implemented by (outer) |
 78: |---|---|---|
 79: | `NoiseProvider` | `src/use_cases/ports.rs` | `SimpleNoiseProvider` |
 80: | `TelemetryPort` | `src/use_cases/ports.rs` | `StdTelemetry` (native stdout), `ConsoleTelemetry` (browser console), `NullTelemetry` (tests) |
 81: | `RendererPort` | `wasm_frontend/application/ports.rs` | `WebGl2Renderer` (browser), recording fakes (tests) |
 82: | `ChunkSourcePort` | `wasm_frontend/application/ports.rs` | `LocalChunkSource` (in-wasm generation); an HTTP-fetching implementation would slot in without touching the engine |
 83: 
 84: ## Data flow: from noise to pixel
 85: 
 86: ```
 87: SimpleNoiseProvider (driver)
 88:       │ NoiseProvider port
 89:       ▼
 90: GenerateChunkArchitectureUseCase ──► VoxelGrid (dense u8 grid + light grid)
 91:       │                                   │
 92:       │                          calculate_voxel_lighting (BFS flood fill)
 93:       ▼                                   ▼
 94: BuildOctreeUseCase ──────────────► SparseVoxelOctree
 95:       │                              (arena Vec<SvoNode>, uniform-collapsed)
 96:       ▼
 97: OctreeGpuSerializer ─────────────► RGBA32UI texel stream, rows of 1024,
 98:       │                              row-padded per chunk
 99:       ▼
100: application::atlas::build_atlas ─► merged atlas + per-chunk rebased roots
101:       │ RendererPort port
102:       ▼
103: WebGl2Renderer ──────────────────► RGBA32UI texture + uniform chunk table
104:       ▼
105: fragment shader (drivers/shaders.rs) — fullscreen quad, sorted chunk AABBs,
106: stack-based SVO march, empty-space skipping ──► pixels
107: ```
108: 
109: Collision geometry is derived **from the same SVO** (solid WALL/RED_WALL
110: leaves → world-space AABBs in `local_chunk_source::extract_collision_boxes`),
111: so physics and visuals can never drift apart. Uniform subtrees collapsed by
112: the SVO become single large collision boxes for free.
113: 
114: ### SVO node texel encoding (RGBA32UI, one node per texel)
115: 
116: | Channel | Internal node (`R == 0`) | Leaf node (`R == 1`) |
117: |---|---|---|
118: | R | 0 | 1 |
119: | G | `child_base_index` (children contiguous at +0..+7) | `voxel_type` |
120: | B | `child_mask` (bit *i* set = child *i* non-empty) | 24-bit `0xRRGGBB` color |
121: | A | 0 | light level 0–15 |
122: 
123: The same layout is documented at its source of truth,
124: `src/adapters/octree_gpu_serializer.rs`, and decoded in
125: `wasm_frontend/src/drivers/shaders.rs` (`decodeNode`).
126: 
127: ## Chunk streaming
128: 
129: Single-threaded wasm has no background meshing thread, so streaming is
130: **time-sliced**: `StreamingPolicy` produces the desired resident set
131: (nearest-first) each frame; the `Engine` loads at most **one chunk per tick**
132: and evicts out-of-range chunks. The atlas texture and collision world are
133: rebuilt only on a resident-set change — steady-state frames upload nothing
134: (asserted by `steady_state_does_not_reupload_atlas`).
135: 
136: Profiles (selected by URL, `?spec=high`):
137: 
138: | | chunk size | radius | voxels | SVO depth |
139: |---|---|---|---|---|
140: | low (default) | 10 u | 1 (3×3) | 0.2 u | 6 |
141: | high | 20 u | 2 (5×5) | 0.1 u | 8 |
142: 
143: The shader's chunk table is fixed at 25 entries — exactly the 5×5 high-spec
144: worst case (`application::atlas::MAX_CHUNKS`).
145: 
146: ## Player simulation
147: 
148: `application::player` ports the original client's tuning 1:1: exponential
149: friction (8 s⁻¹), acceleration 4 u/s² (terminal 0.5 u/s), mouse sensitivity
150: 0.002 rad/px, pitch clamped short of ±90°. Collision is **axis-separated
151: sliding**: X and Z are moved and tested independently against the
152: `CollisionWorld`, so hitting a wall diagonally slides along it. `dt` is
153: clamped to 100 ms so a background-tab hitch cannot teleport the player
154: through a wall.
155: 
156: ## Testing strategy
157: 
158: Ports make the interesting logic natively testable — no browser, no GPU:
159: 
160: - `cargo test --workspace` runs 40 tests: entities, generation, lighting,
161:   octree build/serialize, plus the front end's player physics, sliding
162:   collision, streaming policy/eviction, atlas rebasing, input mapping, and
163:   the resolution governor.
164: - Renderer/chunk-source **test doubles** verify the engine's contract with
165:   its ports (upload counts, draw-table sizes) rather than pixels.
166: - The drivers layer is deliberately thin: translation only, no decisions.
167: 
168: ## Native dev server
169: 
170: `src/main.rs` is a zero-dependency HTTP server used for local development:
171: static files with correct MIME types (`application/wasm` is mandatory for
172: streaming instantiation), plus the legacy JSON/binary chunk endpoints
173: (`/maze`, `/octree`) that the preserved Three.js client (`/legacy`) still
174: consumes. The wasm client needs no data endpoints at all.
175: 
176: ## Roadmap (documented non-goals of this iteration)
177: 
178: - Temporal reprojection / checkerboarding to complement adaptive resolution.
179: - Per-chunk AABB *rasterization* (BackSide boxes + `gl_FragDepth` writeback)
180:   to replace the fullscreen quad once chunk counts grow beyond 25.
181: - Web Worker chunk generation (wasm threads) to remove the 1-chunk/tick cap.
182: - LOD: shallower SVO mip levels for distant chunks.

files.README.md:
1: # Vackrooms
 2: 
 3: A voxel-only rendering engine in Rust, structured with documented Clean
 4: Architecture and compiled to WebAssembly. Procedural "backrooms" world
 5: generation, BFS lighting, sparse voxel octree construction, chunk streaming,
 6: sliding player collision and a WebGL2 hybrid SVO raymarcher all run inside
 7: one ~140 KB wasm module — built to hold up on low-spec hardware.
 8: 
 9: See [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) for the full design (layer map, ports,
10: data flow, texel encodings, streaming and rendering pipeline).
11: 
12: ## Build & run
13: 
14: Prerequisites: Rust (with the `wasm32-unknown-unknown` target) and
15: [`wasm-pack`](https://rustwasm.github.io/wasm-pack/).
16: 
17: ```sh
18: # 1. Build the wasm front end into static/pkg/
19: wasm-pack build wasm_frontend --target web --release --no-typescript --out-dir ../static/pkg
20: 
21: # 2. Run the dev server
22: cargo run
23: 
24: # 3. Open http://localhost:8080
25: ```
26: 
27: Click to capture the mouse; WASD to move, ESC to release.
28: 
29: - `http://localhost:8080/` — wasm engine (low-spec profile: 3×3 chunk
30:   streaming, 0.2 u voxels, adaptive resolution)
31: - `http://localhost:8080/?spec=high` — high-spec profile (5×5 chunks,
32:   0.1 u voxels)
33: - `http://localhost:8080/legacy` — the preserved original Three.js/JS client,
34:   which fetches chunks from the server's `/maze` and `/octree` endpoints
35:   instead of generating them in the browser
36: 
37: ## Tests
38: 
39: ```sh
40: cargo test --workspace
41: ```
42: 
43: The application layers are browser-free by construction, so player physics,
44: collision, streaming, atlas assembly and input mapping are all covered by
45: native unit tests (40 tests at the time of writing).
46: 
47: ## Workspace layout
48: 
49: | Path | What it is |
50: |---|---|
51: | `src/` | `vackrooms` core: entities, use cases, adapters + native dev server |
52: | `wasm_frontend/` | Browser client: application / adapters / drivers (wasm-only) |
53: | `static/` | Thin HTML shell, wasm bundle output (`pkg/`), legacy client |
54: | `wasm_raycaster/` | Legacy CPU raycaster experiment (reference only) |
files.wasm_frontend/src/application/ports.rs:
1: //! Ports (Dependency Inversion boundaries) owned by the application layer.
 2: //!
 3: //! The application layer *defines* these interfaces; the outer layers
 4: //! (adapters / drivers) *implement* them. This keeps the frame loop and
 5: //! streaming logic testable without a GPU or a browser.
 6: 
 7: use crate::application::collision::Aabb;
 8: 
 9: /// Per-chunk data the renderer needs to raymarch one chunk of the SVO atlas.
10: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
11: pub struct ChunkDraw {
12:     /// World-space origin (min corner) of the chunk's SVO cube.
13:     pub origin: [f32; 3],
14:     /// Root node index *within the merged atlas texture*.
15:     pub root_index: i32,
16:     /// Side length of the chunk's SVO cube in world units.
17:     pub world_size: f32,
18: }
19: 
20: /// Camera state for one frame, in world space.
21: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
22: pub struct FrameParams {
23:     pub camera_pos: [f32; 3],
24:     pub yaw: f32,
25:     pub pitch: f32,
26: }
27: 
28: /// Abstraction over the actual rasterizer/raymarcher back end.
29: /// Implemented by `drivers::webgl::WebGl2Renderer` in the browser and by
30: /// test doubles in native unit tests.
31: pub trait RendererPort {
32:     /// Uploads the merged SVO node atlas (RGBA32UI texel stream, 4 u32 per
33:     /// node, rows of 1024 texels — see `OctreeGpuSerializer` in the core).
34:     fn upload_atlas(&mut self, texels: &[u32]);
35: 
36:     /// Draws one frame: fullscreen raymarch of every chunk in `chunks`.
37:     fn draw(&mut self, frame: &FrameParams, chunks: &[ChunkDraw]);
38: }
39: 
40: /// A fully prepared chunk as the application consumes it.
41: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
42: pub struct ChunkPayload {
43:     /// Root node index local to this chunk's `nodes` array.
44:     pub root: u32,
45:     /// GPU-serialized SVO nodes (row-padded, 4 u32 per node).
46:     pub nodes: Vec<u32>,
47:     /// Side length of the SVO cube in world units.
48:     pub world_size: f32,
49:     /// Solid-voxel bounding boxes in world space, for player collision.
50:     pub collision: Vec<Aabb>,
51: }
52: 
53: /// Abstraction over where chunks come from. The browser build implements
54: /// this with in-wasm procedural generation (`adapters::local_chunk_source`);
55: /// a networked build could implement it with HTTP fetches instead.
56: pub trait ChunkSourcePort {
57:     /// Loads the chunk at `origin` for the given Backrooms level
58:     /// (0 = backrooms, 34 = grassland; see the core's `level_generator`).
59:     fn load(&self, origin_x: f32, origin_z: f32, level: u32) -> ChunkPayload;
60: }

1: # wasm_frontend — the browser front end of the voxel engine.
 2: #
 3: # Clean Architecture placement:
 4: #   application/  Use-case layer for the interactive client (player physics,
 5: #                 chunk streaming policy, frame orchestration). Pure Rust,
 6: #                 unit-tested natively. Defines the ports (RendererPort,
 7: #                 ChunkSourcePort) that outer layers implement.
 8: #   adapters/     Interface adapters: input mapping, SVO atlas assembly, and
 9: #                 the local chunk source that drives the `vackrooms` core
10: #                 use cases (generation -> SVO -> GPU serialization).
11: #   drivers/      Frameworks & Drivers: WebGL2 renderer, browser event/rAF
12: #                 plumbing, HUD. Only this layer touches web-sys, and it is
13: #                 compiled exclusively for wasm32.
14: [package]
15: name = "wasm_frontend"
16: version = "0.1.0"
17: edition = "2024"
18: 
19: [lib]
20: crate-type = ["cdylib", "rlib"]
21: 
22: [dependencies]
23: # Inner-ring engine core: entities (VoxelGrid, SparseVoxelOctree),
24: # use cases (GenerateChunk, BuildOctree, lighting) and the GPU serializer.
25: vackrooms = { path = ".." }
26: 
27: # Browser bindings are wasm-only so `cargo test` on the host runs the pure
28: # application/adapters layers without pulling in web-sys.
29: [target.'cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")'.dependencies]
30: wasm-bindgen = "0.2"
31: js-sys = "0.3"
32: console_error_panic_hook = "0.1"
33: web-sys = { version = "0.3", features = [
34:     "Window",

40:     "CssStyleDeclaration",

44:     "MouseEvent",
45:     "Performance",
46:     "CanvasRenderingContext2d",
47:     "ImageData",
48:     "WebGl2RenderingContext",
49:     "WebGlProgram",
50:     "WebGlShader",
51:     "WebGlTexture",
